I'll revert tomorrow (I'm about to go to bed) but I am just confused about whether I should be merging these dependabot PRs, I have no understanding about what they're about.
I suspect this is the issue in #ecosystem infrastructure > ruby version in docgen-action which we never decided on a solution for.

It looks like dependabot just doesn't know your CI uses Ruby 3.1 (due to docgen-action), so it updated this Ruby thing but it dropped support for Ruby 3.1.
So either docgen-action needs to ask for 3.2 or above, or we should figure out how to let dependabot know what's going on.

I think @Marcelo Lynch's idea in the other thread to change docgen-action so that users specify their own ruby version is the "right" solution, but I don't know how disruptive it would be. Better to do it sooner rather than later though, I guess.
Kevin, you already merged the exact same PR two months, got yourself in the same pickle, and got rescued out of it by people here. Why don't you just disable the dependency alerts?

(a) because I thought it might be fixed now (b) because I have no idea how to disable a dependency alert and have no desire to know how (c) because I would prefer to implement the correct solution which the community decides on by asking here rather than taking the bull by the horns and disabling random stuff which I don't understand and which in the long run might make my situation worse.

My failure to merge this broken PR FLT#946 bumping nokogiri to v1.19.3 now manifests itself in a security vulnerability with high severity on the FLT repo. I am not really sure that the security vulnerability ("An attacker able to inject user-supplied text into a CSS selector parse method can cause exponential backtracking, resulting in a potential denial of service.") is something I'm particularly worried about, but it does now result in occasional warnings when I interact with github on the command line.

A graphical rendition of how to DoS FLT is given at the CWE page. During this time I would ask users of the FLT repo to not use any nested quantifiers in their regular expressions :-)

So do I merge FLT#965 or will this break the project? Or should I just try and then revert? I am not really sure what I am supposed to be doing here going forwards (I have no understanding of the importance or role of these auto-generated PRs, all I know is that I am happy to be a guinea-pig for a "downstream of mathlib with no bells and whistles" project).

This one is probably fine. I looked at the diff in the PR summary: https://github.com/lostisland/faraday/compare/v2.14.1...v2.14.2 and coincidentally this shows in .github/workflows/ci.yml that they're testing against ruby 3.1, which is what you're on
